increment_paragraph: **RULE34-PILOT** (pluggable-cards seam B, phase P2, the fifth pilot of GATEWAY-RULE-API-PILOT-MIGRATIONS; [report](../../reports/rule34-pilot/README.md)) adds the rule interface's transfer position (`Position::Transfer`, route map §10, an appended section; `transfer.rs`: `DeclaredEffect`, `Phase`, `TransferQuery`, the vocabulary-free `TransferArm`; route-map order tests in Rust and Python) and moves gateway rule 34 onto it: the element destroyer's order (an unlink of a released parameter applies before the call's own reading) leaves `container_publication::destroyer_split` for the package `crates/gateway-rules/rule-34-element-destroyer` (transfer arm `destroyer-order`, API dependency only), asked by the gateway's `transfer_rules.rs` through the registry switch, which reads an admission fail-closed and splits the operands exactly as before. With `34` off the host's unswitchable guard refuses a call that still declares such an unlink before any of its effects apply (`Unknown`, arguments unresolved, bindings poisoned): its own order would release before unlinking, which rule 34 forbids. Lean `QCore.ElementDestroyerSwitch` (14 audited theorems): the arm's phases are the Rust table, on is `QCore.ElementDestroyer.lower`, off refuses the destroyer, a call without one ignores the switch, off never widens. The card was halted mid-measurement and merged at `62c8e461c`; before the halt its own run against `baseline:80c8aea98` completed system and slice (equal up to a checked bijective revision/digest substitution, 6 and 4 values; 34 off moved nothing there).
